newsitem.title: USA: Signet Banking says it is not for sale.
newsitem.headline: Signet Banking says it is not for sale.

text.p: Signet Banking Corp said on Friday it was not for sale and had not engaged in merger talks.
Responding to market rumors about a merger, Signet said it would continue to pursue its business plan.
Earlier today, traders said the rumors were boosting Signet's stock. The shares were halted at 28-7/8, up 1/8, on volume of 592,700.
The company said it would make no further comment about the rumors and would adhere to a policy of not commenting on rumors.
Stories in Business Week magazine and American Banker described Signet as a takeover target.
Business Week quoted a money manager, whom it did not identify, as saying Signet had rejected a $2.1 billion merger offer from First Union Corp.
Rumors have also mentioned Wachovia Corp as a possible suitor.
A Wachovia spokesman said it was the company's policy not to comment on rumors about mergers or acquisitions.
